summary: Join our training course on Monitoring and Evaluation of Social Protection Programs. Gain essential skills to assess and improve social initiatives effectively.
lede: Monitoring and Evaluation of Social Protection Programs helps practitioners determine whether benefits reach vulnerable households, targeting is accurate, and intended outcomes are being achieved. The course builds practical skills in results frameworks, theories of change, indicator systems, data collection through registries and surveys, and beneficiary verification. Participants also learn to assess program processes, conduct or commission impact evaluations, and produce evidence that supports better decisions. Designed for real-world constraints such as limited budgets, weak data systems, political pressure, and urgent delivery needs, it turns routine activity tracking into a system for learning, accountability, and continuous improvement.
audienceIntro: This course is tailored for professionals across various sectors who are integral to the successful monitoring and evaluation of social protection programs.
audience: Government M&E officers and program managers
Social protection and social safety net program
NGO and development organization program staff
National statistics office and data management professionals
Social registry and beneficiary database managers
modules: Developing Results Frameworks and Theories of Change
Designing Indicator Systems for Social Protection
Process Monitoring and Program Delivery Assessment
Program Integrity, Fraud Detection, and Accountability
Using M&E for Adaptive Management and Policy Learning
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of social protection systems and some experience with monitoring and evaluation processes.
